body.text: Run started 2026-11-17T20:57:56Z (authoritative status). Task understanding: pick 2–3 arbitrary-heading two-blade charger plugs from the right, actively reorient each with opposing fingers while preserving the demonstrated wrist style, place blades up on the left and maintain until 60 s. First 60 minutes are reserved for reconstruction and validation; simulation begins only after that deadline. No target rounds. I will separate video observations from inferred geometry and physics, and use deployment starts without narrowing headings.

Reconstruction camera calibration is weakly constrained by rounded charger corners: unconstrained PnP drifts to weak perspective; a broad MoGe-constrained fit gives f=1050 px and 6.22 px RMS. The supplied pure-rotation background-flow model accumulates 17.8 deg, potentially interpreting handheld translation as rotation. Testing a plane-constrained six-DOF camera fit to frame-0 background correspondences. Segmentation montage inspected: good visible body outlines; white metal blades partly excluded and black entirely hidden near first grasp. Occluded object rotation will remain uncertain/invalid rather than invented.

Dense-frame inspection refines the contact plan: white contact approximately frames 76–211, lift around 110, finger turn around 113–150, placement/release around 180–211; black contact 251–386, lift around 282–290, finger turn 315–333, release around 380. Exact boundaries have 2–4-frame uncertainty. Raw silhouette tracking drifts in depth and produces incorrect blade directions; testing support-constrained static-pose fits and manually feature-seeded tracking before hand fitting. These are reconstruction refinements, not a robot training simulation.

Reconstructed demo scene check: both initially resting chargers remain supported over a 2 s MuJoCo rollout; drift 0.0171 mm each, final translational speeds below 4e-13 m/s. Current visible-mask replay medians are 0.867 (white) and 0.869 (black), with measured hand masks as occluders. Initial and final blade directions visually reviewed. Exact occluded rotations remain inferred and receive broad uncertainty; entirely hidden frames invalid. Human hand fitting is underway using the unchanged mandated MANO fitter. These checks concern only reconstruction geometry.

Default MANO fit is insufficient despite 0.848 mask IoU: validator finds white thumb contact 0%, black opposed contact 31%, and finger self-intersection in 47.5% of visible frames. A nearest-probe contact loss is insufficient. I will retain this baseline with its failures, triangulate the Blender export so signed mesh checks are meaningful, and test a workspace copy of the fitter with explicit thumb-plus-opposing-finger contact and finger separation. Installed fitter code remains unchanged; all added terms and settings will be recorded.

body.text: V4 is format VALID and quality PASS with warnings (r0009). I inspected the comparison views at frames 296 and 300: the visible thumb/index silhouette fits, while the inferred curled fingers below the black body overlap. The validator localizes residual self-intersections to 296, 299–306 and 396, and penetration >5 mm to 288/296. Testing a local refit of black-lift/withdrawal frames with top-k collision losses; all other poses, hand shape and scale frozen so the existing white grasp and wrist reference stay preserved.

Additional physical audit found an object-motion defect beneath the provided continuity thresholds: black centre jumps 73.9 mm at frame 251 (first touch, before observed lift at about 282), and white jumps 27.8 mm at frame 149. This comes from switching static support to a depth-drifting silhouette track, not video evidence. Previous format/quality passes do not establish physical correctness here. Correcting support until lift, smoothly bridging the weakly observed transition and filtering pose jitter, then refitting hands against that corrected scene before the 60-minute deadline.
